extracted.intended_audience: developers/users who need to install Conan 2 (C/C++ package manager) on Windows/Linux/macOS
extracted.subtask_description: Step-by-step installation guidance for Conan 2 on various operating systems, covering recommended methods (pip/pipx), system installers, self-contained executables, and installing from source, plus troubleshooting notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preferred installation method
rubrics_metrics.description: The preferred and strongly recommended way to install Conan is from PyPI, the Python Package Index, using the pip command.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Install latest Conan 2 version using pip: `pip install conan`. This is the recommended approach for most users.

rubrics_metrics.name: Python version requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: To install latest Conan 2 version using pip, you need a Python >= 3.8 distribution installed on your machine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Modern Python distros come with pip pre-installed. If necessary, install pip following pip docs. Make sure that your pip installation matches your Python (>= 3.8) version.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure pip matches Python version
rubrics_metrics.description: Make sure that your pip installation matches your Python (>= 3.8) version.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using the wrong pip (for a different Python interpreter) can install packages to the wrong Python environment. Use virtualenvs or explicit python -m pip to avoid mismatch.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use virtual environments
rubrics_metrics.description: We strongly recommend using virtualenvs (virtualenvwrapper works great) for everything related to Python.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: On Windows, use virtualenvwrapper-win. With Python 3, the built-in module venv can also be used. If not using a virtualenv it is possible that conan dependencies will conflict with previously existing dependencies, especially if you are using Python for other purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Linux global install may need sudo
rubrics_metrics.description: On Linux, you may need sudo permissions to install Conan globally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When installing system-wide (not in a virtualenv) with pip, prefix with sudo or choose `--user` as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: macOS SIP and installation caveat
rubrics_metrics.description: On macOS, especially the latest versions that may have System Integrity Protection, pip may fail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Try using virtualenvs, or install it to the Python user install directory with `pip install --user conan` to avoid SIP-related failures.

rubrics_metrics.name: pip install --user PATH issue
rubrics_metrics.description: When Conan is installed with `pip install --user conan`, a new directory is usually created for it, but the directory is not appended automatically to the PATH and the conan commands do not work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This can usually be solved by restarting the session of the terminal or running `source ~/.profile`. Some Linux distros may require a logout/system restart so Conan is found in the PATH.

rubrics_metrics.name: Updating Conan installed via pip
rubrics_metrics.description: If installed via pip, your Conan version can be updated with `pip install conan --upgrade`.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You might need sudo or `--user`. The upgrade shouldn’t affect the installed packages or cache information. If the cache becomes inconsistent, remove its content by deleting `<userhome>/.conan2`.

rubrics_metrics.name: Externally-managed-environment error and pipx recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: Some modern Linux distributions mark Python installations as 'externally managed', causing errors like `externally-managed-environment` when installing packages with pip.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In those cases, it is recommended to use pipx to install Conan. pipx creates a virtual environment per Python application, isolating Conan and avoiding conflicts with system packages. See PEP-668 for details on this behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Installing Conan with pipx
rubrics_metrics.description: To install Conan with pipx: ensure pipx is installed and on the PATH, then run `pipx install conan`.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: On Debian-based distributions you can install pipx via `apt-get install pipx` and run `pipx ensurepath`. Restart your terminal after ensuring path; then `pipx install conan`. pipx isolates Conan and its dependencies from the system Python.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use system installer or distributed binaries to avoid Python dependency
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a system installer (Homebrew, Debian package, Windows installer, Arch) or distributed Conan binaries to avoid requiring Python on the system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conan downloads page lists installers for macOS Homebrew, Debian, Windows, Arch Linux. Distributed binaries for Windows, Linux, and macOS are available as compressed files that can be uncompressed and run directly.

rubrics_metrics.name: macOS Gatekeeper warning for compressed binaries
rubrics_metrics.description: If using macOS and downloading compressed binaries directly using a web browser, Gatekeeper may quarantine the compressed binaries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To avoid Gatekeeper issues, download binaries using curl, wget, or similar tools rather than via the browser.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create self-contained executable with pyinstaller
rubrics_metrics.description: You can create a self-contained Conan executable (includes Python interpreter and dependencies) using the pyinstaller.py utility in the repo so Python is not required on the system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Process: `git clone https://github.com/conan-io/conan conan_src`; `cd conan_src`; `pip install -e .`; `python pyinstaller.py`. Important: install dependencies and the project first with `pip install -e .` (editable). After creating the executable, it can be uninstalled with pip. The executable must be built on the same platform that will run it because pyinstaller does not cross-build. The resulting executable can be copied to the system PATH.

rubrics_metrics.name: pyinstaller platform limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: pyinstaller does not cross-build; the creation of the self-contained executable has to run on the same platform that will be using the executable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Build the executable on the target OS/architecture. After building, copy the resulting executable into the system PATH of the target machine.

rubrics_metrics.name: Install from source procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: You can run Conan directly from source code by cloning the repository and installing it in editable mode.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clone (folder name matters to avoid import issues): `git clone https://github.com/conan-io/conan.git conan_src`; `cd conan_src`; `python -m pip install -e .`. For the latest development version, checkout the `develop2` branch. Test installation by running `conan` and confirm you see the Conan commands help.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-install session restart on some distros
rubrics_metrics.description: Some Linux distributions (such as Linux Mint) require a restart (shell restart, or logout/system if not enough) after installation so Conan is found in the PATH.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the conan command is not found immediately after installation, restart the terminal session or log out/in (or reboot) as required by the distro.
